facts.statement: Amylodon is an extinct genus of chimaera.
facts.quote: Amylodon is an extinct genus of chimaera.

facts.statement: The genus Amylodon consists of four described species.
facts.quote: It consists of four described species.

facts.statement: The species A. karamysh was named after the Karamysh River near its type locality in Russia.
facts.quote: A. karamysh is known from the latest early Campanian of Russia, the name being derived from the Karamysh River which runs near the type locality.

facts.statement: A. karamysh lived during the latest early Campanian in Russia.
facts.quote: A. karamysh is known from the latest early Campanian of Russia

facts.statement: A. venablesae and A. eocenica lived in England during the Ypresian age.
facts.quote: A. venablesae and A. eocenica are both known from the Ypresian-aged London Clay of England.

facts.statement: All known species of Amylodon are represented mainly by isolated mandibles.
facts.quote: All species are known mainly from isolated mandibles.

facts.statement: Species of Amylodon show a gradual progression toward increased shearing ability.
facts.quote: They show a slow progressing towards increased shearing ability.

facts.statement: While some studies classified Amylodon in Chimaeridae, others assigned it to Edaphodontidae or Rhinochimaeridae.
facts.quote: Amylodon was considered to be a member of Chimaeridae in Nessov and Averianov, 1996 but other studies have either been assigned to the "Edaphodontidae", or to the Rhinochimaeridae.

facts.statement: The parent group of Amylodon is the family Rhinochimaeridae.
Amylodon lived from the Campanian to the Lutetian, between 83.6 and 41.03 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Lutetian (83.6 to 41.03 million years ago)
